citations.narrative:
The facility's acquisition records are incomplete. The acquisition and inventory records did not include the facility's newly
acquired 5 goats and 3 sheep. The acquisition information is also missing for the facility's one highland cow.
Accurate and well-maintained records of acquisition and disposition of animals is critical to identify and trace animals and
to make sure all animals are accounted for.
Every exhibitor shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose acquisition and
disposition information regarding animals purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or otherwise in his or her
possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed of by that
exhibitor. The records shall include any offspring born or hatched.
Correction date: October 1, 2026.

The facility is not keeping the primary enclosure for its two adult rabbits clean and free of hair and cobwebs. Two
inspectors observed excessive accumulation of cobwebs and rabbit fur around the perimeter and underneath the
enclosure. Cobwebs were also seen on the inside corners of the enclosure. There is a trough in the enclosure that is also
discolored and accumulating debris and other waste. The licensee stated this trough is not used for feeding the rabbits.
Cobwebs and excessive animal hair can lead to respiratory disease and is a fire hazard.
Measures were taken to begin cleaning during the inspection. Continue to correct by ensuring the rabbits' primary
enclosure is reasonably free of excreta, hair, cobwebs and other debris.
Correction date: October 1, 2026.

An outdoor enclosure at the facility has inadequate drainage. An enclosure housing one llama and several other non-
regulated animals had a large area surrounding their water trough with standing water and soft, deep mud. Animals in this
enclosure could not access drinking water without walking through muddy or moist conditions.
Excessive time spent in moist substrate may lead to hoof disease or injuries.
The primary water source must be located so that it is accessible at all times without walking through mud. Sufficient
drainage must be in place to allow rapid elimination of excess water.
Correction date: October 16, 2026.

The facility does not have a perimeter fence. Upon arrival, two inspectors observed an arctic fox free-roaming on the
facility’s grounds. There was no employee within eyesight supervising the animal. The licensee stated that a grounds
employee had been asked to supervise the fox. She also stated that although the animal has access to an indoor
enclosure, the fox is let out in the morning to exercise and socialize with the facility’s free-roaming dogs. The fox is
returned to its indoor enclosure in the evening.
Without a perimeter fence, this animal could escape the property or unintentionally interact with outside people or
animals.
All outdoor housing facilities must be enclosed by a perimeter fence that is of sufficient height to keep animals and
unauthorized persons out.
Correction date: November 1, 2026.

Inspectors observed an unclean water receptacle. The water receptacle in an outdoor enclosure housing one llama and
several other non-regulated animals contained cloudy, light brown water and had accumulated green-brown film
throughout the bottom and sides.
Unclean drinking water can lead to contamination and disease, or dehydration if the animals are unwilling to drink it.
Correct by ensuring all water receptacles shall be kept clean and sanitary.
Correction date: October 1, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
